metadata.title: Measurement of Protein Concentration (A280 / BCA / Bradford)
metadata.purpose: Determine the concentration of an unknown protein solution by three independent methods - UV absorbance at 280 nm, the BCA assay, and the Bradford assay - each calibrated against a standard protein, and compare the results.
metadata.scope: Colorimetric/UV protein quantitation of soluble samples against a BSA standard curve, in test tubes/cuvettes (A280, Bradford) and a 96-well plate (BCA). No single assay suits all proteins. Bradford is included for reference (also used in the CK activity assay).
metadata.estimatedTime: ~2-3 h (BCA incubation 15-20 min; Bradford color stable ~1 h)
beforeYouBegin: Run standard samples in duplicate (or triplicate).
Use the 0 mg/mL tube (sample 1) as the blank for spectrophotometer zeroing.
Because the same volume is examined in each assay, plot absorbance directly against standard concentration.
When computing the unknown concentration, multiply by the dilution factor.

materials.name: Bradford working buffer
materials.specification: Acidic Coomassie Brilliant Blue G-250, per tube

steps.action: Prepare 14 test tubes with standards, unknown, and deionized water per Table 1; mix on vortex.
Read A280 in a 1 mL cuvette; zero with sample 1 (0 mg/mL).
Plot A280 vs mg/mL standard; estimate the unknown; calculate A(1%,1cm) at 280 nm.
Prepare BCA working solution: 4 mL Reagent A + 80 uL Reagent B in a 5-mL tube.
Dilute standard BSA to 0.5 mg/mL (500 uL + 500 uL PBS); serial-dilute per Table 2 in duplicate.
Load standards to wells B-G (two columns); load experimental sample: 20 uL, 10 uL+10 uL PBS (1/2), 5 uL+15 uL PBS (1/4).

parameters.rawText: 20 uL experimental sample; 10 uL+10 uL PBS (1/2); 5 uL+15 uL PBS (1/4)

steps.criticalNotes: Dilutions may be pre-made in 1.5-mL tubes.

steps.action: Add 200 uL BCA working solution to each well; incubate; read A562.
Plot the standard curve (A562 vs mg/mL); calculate the unknown.
Dilute standard protein to 0.1 mg/mL (~10 mL).

parameters.rawText: dilute standard protein solution to 0.1 mg/mL for about 10 mL

steps.criticalNotes: Bradford is included for reference (used in CK activity assay).

steps.action: Prepare 17 test tubes per Table 3 (standards/unknown/water) + 3 mL Bradford buffer each; mix on vortex.

parameters.rawText: 3 mL Bradford working buffer per tube

steps.action: Read A595 in a 3 mL cuvette; read low->high protein.

parameters.rawText: color development complete in 2 min, stable up to 1 hour

steps.criticalNotes: Read sequentially to limit dye carryover.

steps.action: Plot ug standard vs A595; estimate the unknown.

controls.name: Blank / zero
controls.description: 0 mg/mL tube (sample 1) for spectrophotometer zeroing in each assay.

controls.name: Standard curve
controls.description: BSA dilution series in each assay (run in duplicate/triplicate).

controls.name: Method comparison
controls.description: Compare A280 vs BCA vs Bradford results and discuss discrepancies.

expectedOutputs: Three standard curves (A280, A562, A595) and the estimated unknown concentration from each.
A(1%,1cm) at 280 nm for the unknown.
A comparison/discussion of the three methods.

troubleshooting.solution: Keep within the series range; re-pipette; use duplicates
Read low->high protein content; rinse cuvette
Choose a suitable standard; report the method; discuss
Multiply diluted wells by the correct dilution factor

safety: BCA Reagent B (Cu2+) and acidic Coomassie dye are irritants - wear gloves; follow disposal rules.
limitations: Each assay depends on amino-acid composition and the chosen standard; only ranges/volumes from the teaching handout are captured. The source's dilution tables are represented compactly in step notes (the schema has no first-class table object - a known limitation).
